summary: The bill requires the Education Department to develop best practices on secure firearm storage and suicide prevention, then mandates school districts receiving certain federal funds to create and annually distribute local guidance on those topics to students, parents, and staff.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the ESEA to mandate distribution of firearm safety guidance by certain LEAs but contains no appropriations, funding authorizations, or spending directives. Any administrative costs would be incidental and minimal. No bearing on government spending levels.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.
The bill references mental health resources and suicide prevention in an educational context but does not alter healthcare delivery, coverage, funding, or policy structures.

The legislation requires schools to distribute best practices on secure firearm storage and suicide prevention, developed with input from ATF, CDC, and others, while including a neutrality clause that neither encourages nor discourages ownership. This constitutes a modest federal push toward safety education often associated with gun-safety initiatives, without imposing new restrictions on possession or sales.
No provisions relate to immigration, visas, border policy, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions concern military budgets, defense programs, or armed forces policy.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.

The bill directly amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act to impose new federal requirements on covered LEAs to develop and distribute firearm-safety guidance annually. This represents a clear expansion of federal involvement in local school curricula and communications.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
